claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a queued execution waiting behind a busy CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each run in turn.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline.
Both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the pipeline to use `QUEUED` mode.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set the pipeline's execution mode and pipeline type.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
A page for the `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource exists at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which prevents concurrent runs from deploying to the same environment.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the stage interacts with an exclusive lock check on the environment it references.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines stage `lockBehavior` property is `runLatest`.

With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually applied.
With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running one update at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The referenced pages exist: /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 queues a second build behind the first, which runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior per stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by the deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on the stage makes queued runs proceed sequentially with the exclusive lock check.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes deployments.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
